You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e8df1a38bd09e0416a1de7006615abfd1c845c9c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Herm=C3=A8s=20B=C3=A9lusca-Ma=C3=AFto?=
 <hermes.belusca-maito@reactos.org>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2020 00:56:33 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] [CONSRV] Fix a corruption of the CONSRV memory when
 converting read input events back to ANSI.

This fixes a 6-year old copy-paste bug introduced by commit b47d51c6 (r64004).
---
 win32ss/user/winsrv/consrv/coninput.c | 5 +++--
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/win32ss/user/winsrv/consrv/coninput.c b/win32ss/user/winsrv/consrv/coninput.c
index 8c2e0e82adb..b4b3061e1a3 100644
--- a/win32ss/user/winsrv/consrv/coninput.c
+++ b/win32ss/user/winsrv/consrv/coninput.c
@@ -564,9 +564,10 @@ ReadInputBuffer(IN PGET_INPUT_INFO InputInfo,
             /* Now translate everything to ANSI */
             if (!GetInputRequest->Unicode)
             {
-                for (; NumEventsRead > 0; --NumEventsRead)
+                ULONG i;
+                for (i = 0; i < NumEventsRead; ++i)
                 {
-                    ConioInputEventToAnsi(InputBuffer->Header.Console, --InputRecord);
+                    ConioInputEventToAnsi(InputBuffer->Header.Console, &InputRecord[i]);
                 }
             }
         }
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a copy-paste error in the loop that processes input events. The original code decremented `NumEventsRead` in the loop condition, which led to incorrect indexing of the `InputRecord` array. This resulted in memory corruption when accessing out-of-bounds elements. The fix changes the loop to use a separate index variable `i` that correctly iterates through the `InputRecord` array without modifying `NumEventsRead`.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a copy-paste error in the loop that processes input events. The original code decremented `NumEventsRead` in the loop condition, which led to incorrect indexing of the `InputRecord` array. This resulted in memory corruption when accessing out-of-bounds elements. The fix changes the loop to use a separate index variable `i` that correctly iterates through the `InputRecord` array without modifying `NumEventsRead`.
